articles.body: In a rare display of intra-party pushback, Robert Corradino, the Republican mayor of Oswego, New York, a city situated along the southern shore of Lake Ontario, has publicly rejected recent political proposals to rename the Great Lake as "Lake America." Robert Corradino, the mayor who never lived anywhere apart from Oswego, said he was taking the issue very personally.“The water is part of our identity,” Corradino said. “Not only our identity, but the economy and the history of the lake are tied to the city.”In an interview with National Post, he said: "We can disagree with the current administration's take about renaming Lake Ontario and still support some of its other initiatives. But we're taking the renaming of the lake very personally in Oswego."President Trump signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America in US government records and maps on August 27 -- in his latest snub to Canada. The change has since been adopted by both Google and Apple Maps for users in the US, but Corradino has said that Oswego does not support the renaming and won't be altering any signage, tourism materials or official communications to reflect the new name."Lake Ontario is in the DNA of Osweganians," he said, adding, "Everything that we are emanates from the lake.""Our tourism from Canada is down substantially. We have stores, we have museums that depend on tourism, and Canadians are a big part of our tourism business," he said.Where is Oswego?Oswego, a city of 17,000, is split between Democrats and Republicans, Corradino said. However, the larger Oswego County is one of the reddest in the state and 61 percent of its voters went for Trump in the 2024 election.Several Oswego County legislators from both parties approved a resolution rejecting the new name, out of concern for the cost of the rebrand on taxpayers and businesses. The resolution said it does not intend to diminish the authority of the federal government, rather it aims to “recognize the longstanding historical and regional significance of the name Lake Ontario.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: France denies inciting failed Niger mutiny, calls accusation ‘pure fantasy’
articles.summary: Niger’s government has widened its blame to unnamed neighbours a week after the assault on a military base.
articles.body:
France has dismissed as “pure fantasy” Niger’s claim that Paris helped incite a mutiny in which soldiers stormed a military airbase and the presidential palace in the capital, Niamey.

French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot made the comment on Saturday, a week after the August 29 assault and a day after Niger’s ruling military council met for the first time since the unrest and repeated its accusations against France.

“This operation, with its international ramifications, was instigated and sustained by a vast network of collusion headed by the French regime of Mr [Emmanuel] Macron,” said Soumana Boubacar, Niger’s government spokesperson, in a statement read out on TV on Friday.

“Traitorous and renegade elements, to whom promises of great things were made, were tasked with carrying out unfulfilled ambitions of Macron and his cronies in our country,” he claimed, saying such “undermining manoeuvres will always fail”.

In response to the accusations, France’s Barrot dismissed the claims and told RFI radio on Saturday: “There never was any intention, nor means that France would have mobilised.”

The exchange marks the latest strain in a relationship that has soured sharply since General Abdourahamane Tchiani seized power in a 2023 coup and turned to Russia for military backing instead of France, Niger’s former colonial power.

The mutiny last week began at Base 101, a military facility inside Niamey’s international airport, when soldiers turned on their commanders and opened fire at several sites in the city.

Fighting spread to the presidential palace and knocked the state broadcaster off air for hours, before Niger’s army, helped by Russian paramilitary fighters known as Africa Corps , retook the base the next day.

State media said hundreds of soldiers took part, and dozens were killed or arrested.

Niger’s government has since widened its accusations beyond France, saying unnamed “African brothers” served as a bridge for the plot, after state television aired a video of an air force captain naming Benin, Chad, Ivory Coast and the regional bloc ECOWAS as backers of the attack.

Benin’s government has rejected the claim, with a spokesman saying “no one in their right mind” believes it.

In that same meeting, Niger’s government acknowledged for the first time that civilians had died in the violence.

That admission came amid a pattern in which Tchiani, who has not appeared in public since the mutiny, has blamed France and other West African states for unrest without producing evidence, which analysts say is aimed more at shaping opinion at home than any legal case.

The pivot to Russia has done little to stop attacks by fighters linked to al-Qaeda and ISIL (ISIS), leaving front-line soldiers who have suffered heavy losses increasingly frustrated, a grievance analysts regard as the true driver of the mutiny.

Relations with Paris have soured further still over Niger’s seizure of uranium assets from French nuclear firm Orano.

articles.title: Colombian government reports three killed in rebel attack on military post
articles.summary: Colombian authorities blame ELN rebel group for attack that reportedly included drones dropping explosives on compound.
articles.body:
Colombian authorities have said that at least three soldiers have been killed and several more injured after an attack on a military compound by an armed group that included drones used to drop explosives.

The Colombian army said on Saturday that the attack had been carried out by the rebel National Liberation Army (ELN) the night before in the municipality of Ocana, which is in the area bordering Venezuela. Two soldiers were killed in the clashes, along with a third who died after receiving medical attention. Four were injured.

“To the ELN I say with absolute clarity: for every police officer or soldier you kill, I will bring down on you the full weight and legitimate force of the State,” President Abelardo de la Espriella said in a statement on social media condemning the attack.

Authorities said that drones dropped explosives onto the compound in the department of Norte de Santander before fighting took place within the facility. The news service AFP reported that at least 20 drones loaded with explosives were utilised in the attack, citing an unnamed security official.

De la Espriella won office pledging to return Colombia to militarised confrontation with armed groups and criminal organisations that have jostled for influence across the country, despite concerns that it could lead to surging violence and possible rights abuses.

Deadly attacks by armed groups have continued to rattle the country since his inauguration.

The attack on Friday took place in the northeastern Catatumbo region, where the ELN is based and where the government has carried out military raids against armed groups.

De la Espriella has also promised closer ties with the United States, which has sought to expand its military involvement in the region under the so-called “Shield of the Americas” initiative.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is set to meet with de la Espriella, a former lawyer who previously represented leaders of paramilitaries, in the Caribbean city of Barranquilla next week.

articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The Centre has decided to advance the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 in Uttar Pradesh, Goa, Punjab and non-snow-bound areas of.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Centre has decided to advance the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 in Uttar Pradesh, Goa, Punjab and non-snow-bound areas of Uttarakhand — given that all four states are due for assembly polls early next year — to the time period December 1, 2026 to January 4, 2027, with January 5, 2027 as the reference date. This will be preceded by a 15-day self-enumeration window in the four states from November 16 to 30, 2026.The first phase of Census in Manipur, which is also due for assembly polls in February-March next year, was recently postponed in view of demands from within the state to hold the national register of citizens (NRC) exercise first.The advancing of the population enumeration phase in the four other poll-bound states will avert the logistical challenges that may have arisen on account of a clash between the usual timeline for census and the assembly elections. Both elections and census rely on the same pool of govt employees — largely teachers — for their conduct.Conventionally, the second phase of census — involving population enumeration — is held countrywide, other than in snow-bound areas of a few states/Union territories, in the month of February, with March 1, as the reference date.The population enumeration phase in the snow-bound areas of Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, J&K and the whole of Ladakh is currently underway and will be completed by the end of this month."The conduct of Census of the population shall be undertaken in the states of Goa, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and areas other than snow-bound areas of the State of Uttarakhand, from December 1, 2026 to January 4, 2027 with a revisional round from January 5, 2027 to January 9, 2027,” the home ministry stated in a notification issued late on Saturday.Five states — Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Goa and Manipur — are set to go to polls in February-March next year. While the term of the Manipur assembly is expiring on March 13, 2027, that of Goa assembly ends on March 14, 2027; Punjab assembly on March 16, 2027; Uttarakhand assembly on March 28, 2027; and Uttar Pradesh assembly on May 22, 2027.Census 2027, apart from being the first 'digital' census, will capture 'caste' for the first time since 1931.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Cubans and Afghans deported from US arrive in Guyana
articles.summary: Guyana‘s government said Saturday it has received the first of six deportees from the United States under the Trump administration’s third-country deportation program.
articles.body: GEORGETOWN, Guyana — Guyana’s government said Saturday it has received the first of six deportees from the United States under the Trump administration’s third-country deportation program. Guyana’s Foreign Secretary Robert Persaud said the six nationals from Cuba and Afghanistan arrived in the South American country Friday after being vetted by his administration and found to have no criminal background. He added the group was kicked out of the U.S. primarily because of immigration issues. Persaud said his administration reached an agreement to host the deportees after months of negotiations. He also told The Associated Press that “the U.S. has not made any further requests.” The arrangement will run for a year and does not constitute permanent resettlement, he said. Those relocated to Guyana under the Assisted Voluntary Return Program will await the outcome of their immigration status determination while in Guyana. They could ultimately return to their country of origin or be relocated somewhere else. The U.N. International Organization for Migration is responsible for implementing the program, authorities in Guyana said, adding that the government will not bear any housing or supporting costs. Guyana, a founding member of the 15-nation Caribbean Community, is the latest of several member states to have received small groups of U.S. deportees. Others include St. Kitts and Nevis, Belize and St. Lucia, which was due to accept its first group this week, officials said.

articles.title: Meet Andy Barrett, the 13-year-old Ohio student who turned a school 3D printer into a small business, selling 150 fidget toys and raising money for epilepsy awareness
articles.summary: US News: Most 13-year-olds walk into middle school tech lab thinking about passing their next assignment or making something cool to toss into their backpack. .
articles.body: Most 13-year-olds walk into middle school tech lab thinking about passing their next assignment or making something cool to toss into their backpack. Andy Barrett, an eighth-grader at Granville Middle School in Ohio, saw something entirely different when he looked at his school's 3D printer. He saw an opportunity to build a business that could actually help people. Armed with basic design software, brightly colored plastic filament, and a personal drive to make a difference, Andy launched a micro-business right from his classroom. He designed, printed, and sold roughly 150 custom fidget toys to fellow students, teachers, and neighbours. Instead of pocketing the money for video games or new shoes, he directed every cent of his profits toward epilepsy awareness and research.From classroom tool to business ideaThe project began inside a standard technology and engineering class, the kind of room where students typically learn the basics of digital design and manufacturing. In most middle schools, a 3D printer gets used to produce simple trinkets, small keychains, or prototype parts for short-term grading rubrics. Andy realised early on that the technology offered far more potential. He noticed how popular fidget toys had become among his peers. Kids were constantly looking for tactile objects to help them focus, manage stress, or simply keep their hands occupied during long school days. Rather than buying mass-produced plastic toys from big store shelves, Andy figured he could design his own versions, customise them, and offer them directly to people around him.Designing and printing the toysBringing a digital design to life takes far more work than simply hitting print. After getting approval from his teachers, Andy spent long hours in the school lab perfecting his fidget toys. He learnt the software from scratch, playing around with different shapes, hinges and textures, so the finished pieces felt comfortable to hold. The learning curve was sharp. He'd tackle clogged nozzles, peeling plastic, and failed prints tossed into the scrap bin. After printing, each piece required a bit of handwork, like trimming away excess material or smoothing out any rough spots. Andy relied on his friends to test early prototypes, modifying his designs according to their feedback until the toys were rugged and dependable.Selling 150 fidget toysWhen the other kids saw the bright, custom toys in action, word spread through the hallways in a hurry. What began as a few casual sales has turned into a steady stream of orders, with teachers, school staff and neighbours getting in on the act. Andy quickly found himself running a real business, keeping track of customers and money, fitting in printing time around his classes. When he finally hit his goal of selling 150 toys, he had built a functioning, thriving business right out of his middle school science lab.Why epilepsy awareness?What truly set Andy apart was his motivation. From the very beginning, he decided that the proceeds would go directly to funding epilepsy research and supporting organisations that help families dealing with the condition. The choice was deeply personal. Andy knows people in his life who have epilepsy, a neurological disorder that causes unpredictable, recurring seizures. Seeing friends or family struggle with the difficulties of the condition gave him a clear view that it can be hard. In addition to the physical toll of medical appointments and daily medications, people with epilepsy often face social stigma, anxiety and a general lack of understanding from those around them. Andy saw his fidget toys as a creative way to start conversations, educate his peers and create meaningful support for a cause that doesn’t get enough attention in middle school halls.Profits into impactAndy turned profits into donations and simple plastic gadgets into tools for social good. While the dollar figure alone was an impressive accomplishment for an eighth-grader, the educational impact went so much deeper. Every transaction became a moment to talk about epilepsy. Classmates who bought a toy were not just getting a fun accessory for their desk, they were learning about a neurological condition that affects millions of children and adults worldwide. Andy proved that you do not need a massive corporate budget to make a meaningful difference in your community.Support from school and familyProjects like this rarely succeed in a vacuum. Andy’s initiative flourished because his surrounding community chose to champion his effort. His teachers provided the trust, classroom access, and flexibility needed to run the 3D printers during free hours. His family helped him plan the sales, manage the money responsibly and donate the proceeds to real non-profits. His friends and neighbours showed up as excited customers. This collaborative spirit shows what’s possible when schools and communities support young people to pursue true passion projects.What’s next for Andy?Andy is 13 years old and still in middle school. He has many years of learning and experimentation ahead of him. He could keep selling fidget toys. He could expand into other 3D-printed products. Or he could channel his energy into new causes and new projects. Whatever he does next, he’ll take experience of running a small, purpose-led company with him. The 150 fidget toys he sold and the money he raised for epilepsy awareness are real proof right now that even one student can use a classroom tool for good, if he has the right support and motivation.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: No room to be kind: US immigration judges told to reduce time for people awaiting Green Card before being deported
articles.summary: US News: A Guardian report claimed that immigration judges across the US have been asked to be strict and deny people time as they wait for their Green Cards s.
articles.body: A Guardian report claimed that immigration judges across the US have been asked to be strict and deny people time as they wait for their Green Cards so that they can be deported. A mandatory training for judges also urged them to threaten attorneys who accept too many immigration cases. “There is no room to be kind; there is only urgency to make them leave [the US], one way or the other," the judges were told.Citing sources, the Guardian report claimed that hundreds of immigration judges attended a mandatory presentation in recent days about “continuances” – a legal tool which has historically been used to give immigrants more time to find lawyers, build their cases or wait for approval of their applications for documents at another federal immigration agency.The virtual training session was led by a veteran immigration judge, Keith Hunsucker, of the Board of immigration appeals, the immigration courts’ appellate branch. He denied over 80% of asylum cases for much of the time that he was on the bench in immigration court before moving on to other roles, the report said.The training was apparently meant to reduce the immigration court backlog and they were taught that some continuances are sought solely for the purpose of delay and persons illegally present in the United States who wish to remain have a substantial incentive to prolong litigation so they may avoid deportation as long as possible.Continuance requests solely for dilatory purposes should not be countenanced by Immigration Judges,” one slide readAn approved visa petition should not delay deportation proceedings if the visa itself is not yet available because of annual quotas but would be issued to the qualified recipient at a later, albeit unspecified, date, the training suggested.Though there is a huge backlog, the judges were told during the training that immigration attorneys risk punitive measures for accepting what are deemed too many cases. “Where a practitioner takes on more cases than he or she can responsibly and professionally handle,” one of the slides read, “it may be appropriate for an Immigration Judge to consider referral to EOIR disciplinary counsel for further action and possible sanction for a violation.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: At least 22 people were killed and several others injured after a fire broke out at a wedding party in Kinshasa, the capital of the Democratic Republic of Congo, a regional mayor said on Saturday.The fire started late Friday night and continued into the early hours of Saturday at a building in Lingwala, northern Kinshasa. The building’s narrow hallways became congested as people tried to escape the blaze, as cited by AP.Several victims, both alive and dead, were taken to the roadside as attendees attempted to help those who survived.Lingwala Mayor Norbert Mushinga told the Congolese Press Agency that the provisional death toll stood at 22, adding that it could rise further.The exact cause of the fire remained unconfirmed. “It is a tragedy,” Jacquemin Shabani, Congo’s deputy prime minister and interior minister, said. Shabani visited the site on Saturday morning.Deadly fires are common in densely populated parts of Kinshasa, where urban development often takes place without adequate fire services and other safety provisions. Local media reported that several fires have occurred in the city this year, particularly during the dry season.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: How much jail time is YouTuber Jack Doherty facing after Florida domestic battery arrest?
articles.summary: US Streamers News: YouTuber Jack Doherty could face up to one year in county jail if he is found guilty of a domestic battery charge in Florida. The 22-year-old creator .
articles.body: YouTuber Jack Doherty could face up to one year in county jail if he is found guilty of a domestic battery charge in Florida. The 22-year-old creator was arrested in Fort Lauderdale on September 4 after police responded to a reported domestic dispute. Police said Doherty and a woman got into a physical fight inside a home. The woman was reportedly not hurt. Doherty was taken to Broward County Main Jail, and his bond was later set at $1,000.Jack Doherty could face up to one year in jailUnder Florida law, battery is usually treated as a first-degree misdemeanor. If Doherty is convicted of the charge he currently faces, the maximum punishment can be one year in county jail.He could also receive a fine of up to $1,000. However, these are the highest punishments allowed by law. They do not mean that Doherty will definitely receive one year in jail or a $1,000 fine.Florida law can also require at least one year of probation in domestic violence cases. A person who is found guilty, receives withheld adjudication or pleads no contest may also have to complete a batterers’ intervention program.There is also a separate rule about jail time for some first domestic violence offenses. It can require at least 10 days in jail when a person is found guilty and is found to have intentionally caused bodily harm.However, police said the woman involved in Doherty’s case was not injured. Because of this, the information currently available does not show that this 10-day minimum would apply to his case.YouTuber Jack Doherty arrested on Florida domestic battery chargePolice said officers went to the Riverside Park area of Fort Lauderdale at about 11:56 a.m. on September 4 after receiving a report of a domestic dispute.According to police, early information suggested that Doherty and a woman had a physical dispute inside a residence. The woman was not reported to have suffered injuries.Doherty was then booked into Broward County Main Jail. His bond was set at $1,000, and he was ordered not to contact the woman.The arrest is not Doherty’s first recent legal problem. In 2025, he was arrested in Miami Beach on drug possession and resisting arrest charges. That case was later resolved through a deferred prosecution program and did not result in a conviction.A source close to Doherty reportedly told TMZ that the YouTuber acted in self-defense. Doherty has not made a direct public statement about the latest arrest, and no trial date has been announced.For now, Doherty is facing a misdemeanor domestic battery charge. While the law allows up to one year in county jail, the final outcome will depend on how the case moves through court.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Fantastic' moment blind Abergavenny veteran, 95, drives again
articles.summary: Jim Alison, who gave up his licence five years ago, has driven again with support from a charity.
articles.body:
A 95 year-old veteran has spoken of his joy at driving again, five years after he was registered blind and had to give up his licence.

Jim Alison, from Abergavenny, raced around Llandow Circuit in the Vale of the Glamorgan as part of a charity event which helps people with disabilities to experience driving.

"I think I managed to get to 90 km/ph (55mph)," said Jim, a former chauffeur, who drove alongside an instructor with dual controls.

"You put your life in their hands and it was absolutely fantastic," added Jim, who served with the Royal Engineers for 22 years before becoming a driver in London.

"They let me take over for a while going down the straight because, being sight impaired, I couldn't see the bends. "

He said he never thought he would be able to drive again after his eyesight deteriorated due to macular degeneration.

Jim was part of a group from Blind Veterans UK who took part in the Speed of Sight event at the circuit near Cowbridge, Vale of Glamorgan.

The event allows people of all ages and backgrounds to experience the thrill of driving.

Harley, 14, who has a visual impairment, went around the track for a second time, having first done so when he was 10.

"It's like happiness, excitement, wonder - it all goes through your mind in a blur because, literally, you're going so fast."

He said it was a "good experience" for disabled children and adults, particularly those who love motorsports.

"You get a rush of adrenaline and you just feel really excited."

Speed of Sight is a charity founded by Mike Newman, a motorsports fan who was born blind and told his dreams of being a racing driver were impossible.

But that did not stop him, going on to secure a number of world records for driving and in 2012 he set up his charity, a response to the many people he met who missed driving after having to give up their licences.

"Because I love cars so much myself, I tried to think of an idea of how we could get behind the wheel again and make it fun and exciting," said Mike.

"It opens up the opportunities of complete enjoyment, forgetting the day-to-day challenges that you're having to having to cope with.

"Or, if I can drive a car on a racetrack, what other things can be enjoyed."

The cars used are modified Maxda MX5s with dual controls with names like Stanton and Baxter, a nod to some of the guide dogs which have lived with Mike over the years.

Many of the participants are what the instructors jokingly call "repeat offenders", including Dean Twaite from Tredegar who drove army vehicles as a member of Royal Corps of Transport in the 1970s and 1980s.

Dean, 68, lost his sight in an industrial accident and has not had a driving licence since 2007.

"It was a bit frightening because I can't see in front of me. But the instructors, they were marvellous," said Dean, who explained he was given one tap on the leg to speed up and two to brake.

"Feeling the wind in the face like that was exhilarating - it was really great, really great," added Dean, who said the experience brought back a freedom and confidence he couldn't describe

"There's no such thing as can't. If you put your mind to it, you can do it."

articles.title: Prince William to attend King Harald's funeral in Norway
articles.summary: The Prince of Wales will represent the King at the funeral of Harald V in Oslo next week.
articles.body:
The Prince of Wales will attend the funeral of King Harald V of Norway on Wednesday in Oslo, Buckingham Palace has announced.

Also going to the funeral, in a personal capacity, is Princess Anne, who is godmother to Norway's new monarch, King Haakon VIII.

The late King Harald, a popular, modernising figure who had been on the Norwegian throne for 35 years, died last month at the age of 89.

Royal sources say Prince William's attendance, representing his father King Charles, follows the convention that the monarch does not usually go to the funeral of another head of state.

Large crowds are expected for the farewell to King Harald on 9 September, with a funeral procession to be followed by a service at Oslo Cathedral.

Thousands have queued to pay their respects to the late king, during his lying in state in the chapel of the Royal Palace in the Norwegian capital.

At the funeral, alongside Prince William, will be the widowed Queen Sonja, members of the Norwegian royal family including new King Haakon VIII, and other European royals.

The service will be followed by a private burial in Norway's royal mausoleum in the Akershus Fortress.

Among the tributes to King Harald was an emotional televised speech by his son King Haakon, who said: "Thank you for being such a good dad."

Harald had been seen as a down to earth "people's king" who had helped to modernise the monarchy, broken with tradition by marrying a commoner and served as a unifying figure.

His son said he represented the values of a "society built on law and justice, where everyone is of equal value".

King Charles's message praised his cousin King Harald for serving his people with "unwavering dedication, guiding Norway through times of great change with warmth and humility".

King Haakon assumes his role at a difficult time, with the Norwegian royal family facing scandals this year.

His wife, Queen Mette-Marit, came under scrutiny when it was revealed she had maintained a three-year friendship with the sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, for which she publicly apologised.

Her son from a previous relationship, Marius Borg Høiby, was convicted in June of rape and other offences and sentenced to four years in prison. He is appealing.

While Prince William will be in Norway, King Charles has returned to Scotland, after meeting President Macron of France at the Bayeux Tapestry exhibition in London this week.

The King will be hosting Andy Burnham at Balmoral this weekend, in the traditional annual visit of the prime minister to stay with the monarch.

articles.title: Border Policeman killed in Netanya shooting, culprit suspected to be IDF soldier
articles.summary: According to police reports, it remains unclear what led the suspect, who is reportedly currently serving in the military, to open fire at police officers. B...
articles.body:
A man was shot dead in Netanya after reportedly firing his weapon during an unclear shooting incident, with the suspect believed to be an IDF soldier currently serving in the military.

Border Police officer Sergeant David Hoyer Amrani, 20, was killed in the shooting, which took place in the Kiryat Hasharon area of Netanya, with the shooter's motives remaining unclear as police continue their investigation.

In separate incidents, a stabbing attack occurred in Jaffa, Tel Aviv, and a 21-year-old resident of Herzliya was arrested on suspicion of involvement in a shooting in a residential building lobby, with investigations ongoing in both cases.

According to police reports, it remains unclear what led the suspect, who is reportedly currently serving in the military, to open fire at police officers.

Border Police officer Sergeant David Hoyer Amrani, 20, was shot and killed in the Kiryat Hasharon area of Netanya on Saturday

An unidentified suspect, who is suspected to be an IDF soldier per Israeli media reports, opened fire at a police unit and was neutralized by officers at the scene, according to a statement from the Israel Police.

Central District Commander Deputy Commissioner Amir Cohen went to the scene of the crime, along with other police units, once it became clear that the situation was unusually violent.

The shooter's motives are unclear, according to police , who were still at the initial stages of investigation at press time.

Sgt. Amrani was a resident of Netanya and had joined the Judea and Samaria Border Police in August 2024 for his compulsory military service, operating primarily in Hebron. Eight months before his death, he transferred to another company within the Judea and Samaria Border Police. He is survived by his parents and siblings.

Later on Saturday, Police issued a statement on a reported stabbing attack in Jaffa, Tel Aviv.

The victim, a man in his 40's according to Hebrew media reports, was evacuated by Magen David Adom (MDA) paramedics to Wolfson Medical Center in Holon.

Police officers from the Jaffa station arrived at the scene shortly after the attack and began investigating and collecting evidence, including searching for suspects.

The circumstances of the incident are under investigation.

Herzliya shooting in residential building

On Friday, a 21-year-old resident of Herzliya was arrested on suspicion of involvement in a shooting that occurred in the lobby of a residential building in the city center, according to a police statement.

When police officers arrived at the scene, they discovered evidence in the lobby consistent with gunfire.

Following their initial investigation, the suspect was located and taken into custody on Friday afternoon.

During the arrest, authorities found a scooter without a license plate near the suspect's location, which they believe may have been used in the shooting.

The suspect is currently being questioned and is expected to appear in court on Saturday evening for a hearing regarding the police's request to extend his detention.

The investigation into the circumstances surrounding the shooting is ongoing.

Jerusalem Post Staff contributed to this report.

articles.title: TV presenter Sarah Khalifa sentenced to death in Egypt drugs case
articles.summary: Sarah Khalifa is best known for her TV programme Mission Impossible which dealt with crime issues.
articles.body:
Egyptian television presenter Sarah Khalifa and 11 other people have been sentenced to death by hanging after being convicted of drugs charges.

According to state-owned al-Akhram newspaper, they were part of a criminal gang which imported ingredients used to make drugs with the intent of selling them.

They also had illegal firearms and munitions.

Khalifa, 39, is best known for her TV programme Mission Impossible which dealt with crime issues. She has denied the charges.

The verdict - which can be appealed against - was first announced last month.

However, it was only confirmed a month later after the court obtained a religious opinion from the grand mufti of Egypt - a legal requirement in death sentence cases.

During the trial, the court heard that authorities had seized more than 750kg (1,653lbs) of narcotics and the imported raw materials to make them.

Twenty witnesses had given statements to the prosecutors, al-Akhram said, in addition to electronic evidence that included conversations and video clips.

According to the state-run Akhbar al-Youm newspaper, when asked by the judge about her alleged role during a court appearance last September, Khalifa said she had never seen any drugs until she was photographed with them inside the anti-narcotics authority offices.

The defendants were found guilty of drug trafficking and rape, "crimes that did not amount to 'intentional killing' to which the use of the death penalty must be restricted under international law and standards", the report said.

articles.title: 10 days after Nepal flash floods, woman, Chinese man rescued
articles.summary: South Asia News: KATHMANDU: Two people were rescued alive from separate flood-hit sites on Saturday, 10 days after Bhote Koshi-Trishuli flood in Nepal. Chandika Kumari.
articles.body: KATHMANDU: Two people were rescued alive from separate flood-hit sites on Saturday, 10 days after Bhote Koshi-Trishuli flood in Nepal. Chandika Kumari Shrestha, 64, was found semi-conscious on the upper floor of a four-storey house buried under debris in Betrawati, Nuwakot district, while her family had already given up hope and started symbolic funeral rites in Kathmandu.In Rasuwa, Chinese worker Luhaitao was pulled out alive from Audit 4 tunnel of Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project, around 225 metres inside the tunnel.Nepal police said a nine-member team led by inspector Suman Kumar BK rescued Chandika from the house, which officials identified as belonging to Anand Shrestha. She was first taken by helicopter to Nepal Army's Maithili Barracks in Trishuli Bazaar for initial treatment and later shifted to Birendra Military Hospital in Kathmandu. Officials said she had wounds under her feet. Her son, Ashish Shrestha, said the family's own home stood near the suspension bridge in Betrawati before the flood struck. "The flood washed it away," Ashish said. "Only my parents were at home at the time. My father has not been found yet."Relatives said the four-storey house was swept from its original location and lodged near Trishuli bank, but rescuers and family members could not reach it for days because the area had turned into a swamp of mud, debris and decomposing bodies. Her son-in-law and other family members searched Betrawati and Trishuli banks for two to three days, while Ashish kept returning to the area where the house had stood but couldn't go in."We searched a lot for eight days," relative Rameshman Shrestha said. "After not finding them anywhere, we gave up hope." The family then gathered at a rented house in Sano Bharyang, Kathmandu, and began symbolic funeral rites and preparations for cremation without her body. "The whole family consulted, and it was decided to perform the funeral rites," Rameshman said.He said one thought continued to trouble him even after the rituals began. "If she was inside a house, maybe she had gone upstairs and eaten whatever she found," he said.The last rites were already underway when relatives received word that Chandika had been found alive.Betrawati remains one of the worst-hit settlements along Trishuli corridor. Local officials said only five of around 300 houses were left standing after the flood.In Rasuwa, Luhaitao was rescued around noon by a joint team of Nepal army personnel and South Korean experts and flown to Birendra Military Hospital, where representatives of the Chinese embassy later inquired about his condition.Videos from the site showed rescuers trying to establish his identity after he was brought out. When asked whether he was Nepalese, he remained silent; when asked whether he was Chinese, he appeared to respond in the affirmative. articles.title: With bare hands, lone warrior cleans up dumpyard of a river
articles.summary: India News: BHOPAL: His online followers know him as 'Bittu Tabahi'. In reality, Surendra Singh Choudhary is the exact opposite of what the moniker 'Tabahi', mean.
articles.body: BHOPAL: His online followers know him as 'Bittu Tabahi'. In reality, Surendra Singh Choudhary is the exact opposite of what the moniker 'Tabahi', meaning destruction, implies.For the past seven months, this 21-year-old BSc student has been a solitary warrior against civic mess and pollution in his hometown, Biaora in MP's Rajgarh district, picking up plastic bottles, tangled weeds and other solid waste from Ajnar river, which had virtually become a dumpyard.With no heavy machinery or protective gear at his disposal, he removed the garbage with his bare hands, often at great risk to his health.Bittu's dogged pursuit has helped restore a section of the river, earning him widespread praise across the country and an invite from CM Mohan Yadav Saturday. They had a warm exchange at the CM's residence in Bhopal, where Yadav assured Bittu of every possible support from govt.The chief minister also shared a video on X, calling Bittu a "son of Biaora" who not only restored Ajnala (the river stretch passing through Biaora) to its original form through sheer resolve and effort, but also sent out a larger message that one man's determination is all it takes to bring meaningful change.There were also reports that the CEO of an organisation from the Netherlands had offered him a job, but Bittu said he had only heard this from media reports. "I am yet to receive any information about it first hand," he told TOI.Encouraged by his success, Bittu, whose parents work in the health department, has decided to expand his work. "My sole objective is to keep my hometown clean. I have decided to take my work to other public places," he said.Bittu started his mission on Republic Day this year. Upset that everyone complained about the mess, but none - including the municipal administration - addressed it, the college-goer decided to get his hands dirty. From removing garbage piles on streets to pulling out weeds from water bodies, his activism eventually drew national attention.Unfortunately, his selfless service is being undone by the same people he is trying to help. In his interaction with the chief minister, Bittu shared the pain of watching people throw garbage into the river again, oblivious to the effort that went into cleaning it. "I don't know why people keep dumping waste into the river," he said, his voice betraying anger.The silver lining is that the local municipal corporation has now woken up to its civic mandate, and has deployed JCBs and Poclain machines to clear waste piles from the streets. However, the larger problem - habitual littering and a lack of collective ownership - remains unaddressed.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
